extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural community (applicants, awardees, peer reviewers, institutional grants offices, and advisory council members)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH notice describing what extramural stakeholders (applicants, grantees, reviewers, institutions) should do and expect during a lapse in federal appropriations, including submission, review, award, reporting, payment, and animal welfare procedures. It explains which systems remain accessible, which activities continue or pause, and recommended actions to document issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to award types
rubrics_metrics.description: This Notice applies to grants, cooperative agreements, and other transaction awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA systems availability and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA systems will be operational, but with limited support and use restricted to excepted activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA will provide limited end-user support only for excepted/approved staff and excepted programs. The eRA service desk will not be fully operational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting system issues for late-application consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicants encounter system issues when applying, they should submit an eRA service desk ticket to document the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will take documented issues into consideration for accepting late applications when operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail, phone, fax, and postal mail unavailability
rubrics_metrics.description: During the funding lapse, NIH extramural employees are prohibited from working, so there will be no access to voice mail, e-mail, fax, or postal mail; mail requiring signature may not be received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended that you delay sending such communications until after operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central policy/compliance e-mail boxes unoperational
rubrics_metrics.description: For the duration of the funding lapse, all central e-mail boxes and web ticketing systems for questions related to NIH grants policy and compliance will not be operational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human participant safety emergency contact
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of an emergency involving human participant safety in NIH-funded research, contact Dr. Jon Lorsch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information is provided in the Notice for immediate safety-related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue to submit applications to posted due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should continue to submit applications in accordance with the due dates outlined in the Notices of Funding Opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be accepted (e.g., Grants.gov, ASSIST) but will not be processed by NIH until operations resume; plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov acceptance vs NIH processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov will be open and can accept electronic applications, but applications will not be processed by NIH until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASSIST availability for multi-project applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The ASSIST system will remain available and can accept multi-project applications, but applications will not be processed by NIH until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial peer review meetings suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: During the funding lapse, NIH will not be able to conduct initial peer review meetings—whether in-person or via teleconference or other electronic media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operations resume, meetings will be re-scheduled and pending applications processed and reviewed as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed release of peer review results
rubrics_metrics.description: Final impact scores and summary statements from reviews that occurred prior to shutdown may not be available until operations resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should monitor national news for resumption of government operations and then check the NIH website for updates on extended or re-scheduled meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access to IAR and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who agreed to serve on review panels scheduled during the lapse will have access to the Internet Assisted Review (IAR) site and may upload initial critiques and initial scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support for IAR will not be available; reviewers scheduled to travel will not be able to board and will receive instructions about reservations; SROs will contact reviewers with details after operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Council review suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not be able to conduct Advisory Council review meetings during the funding lapse; review-support systems will not be operational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No applications will be processed for Council review or taken to Council meetings during that time; meetings will be re-scheduled when operations resume and Executive Secretary will contact members with details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active grant work may continue
rubrics_metrics.description: For the duration of the funding lapse, all work and activities performed under currently active NIH grant awards may continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, many reporting and administrative functions will be limited or delayed as described elsewhere in the Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR submission requirements during lapse
rubrics_metrics.description: For annual or final Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) due during the funding lapse, eRA Commons will be available and users must submit reports on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH staff will review RPPRs after operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Award (NoA) processing suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for excepted programs, no NIH grant awards will be processed for the duration of the funding lapse; awards with an issue date during the lapse will not be sent to recipients until operations resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will not affect the start date or the issue date of awards — only when the award document is sent/available in eRA Commons. Institutions may use pre-award costs authority at their own risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-cost extension (NCE) submissions and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons will remain accessible but staff will not be available to review and approve NCE requests during the lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should submit NCE notifications in accordance with standard requirements; requests for second and greater NCEs (which require prior approval) may be submitted but will not be reviewed until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: General access to eRA Commons and OER-supported systems
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons and other OER-supported systems will be accessible for viewing and processing certain actions (viewing submitted applications, IAR access, Commons Registration, xTrain, Closeout documents, FCOI notifications, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited staff support will be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval requests and other communications delay
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH extramural employees will have no access to voice mail or e-mail during the funding lapse, so all prior approval requests and other communications will not be received until operations resume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is recommended you delay sending such communications until after operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to PSC/PMS and drawdowns during lapse
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of awards received prior to the lapse may continue drawing funds during an appropriations lapse; the Payment Management System (PMS) will remain operational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing internal controls will continue, but recipients of awards with restrictive terms and conditions or requests that trigger PMS edit checks and/or drawdown limit controls may not be able to drawdown funds. Recipients can continue to complete and submit Federal Financial Reports (FFR) in PMS, but NIH staff will not review/process FFRs until operations resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend the Spend activities continue
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will continue to process Defend the Spend requests, on a daily basis, during the appropriations lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: OLAW operations and animal welfare reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare (OLAW) business processes are funded by annual appropriations and are not excepted; no OLAW mission activities will continue during the funding lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are encouraged to delay sending Assurance documents, reports of noncompliance, or IACUC suspension reports to OLAW until operations resume. OLAW will extend deadlines for reporting activities as necessary. Institutions remain responsible for local oversight and ensuring animal welfare and compliance during the lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of contact for inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct inquiries related to the Notice to the Office of Policy for Extramural Research Administration (OPERA), Office of Extramural Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact email provided in the Notice for further questions after operations resume.
